headline: Scientists Find Natural 'Off Switch' for Inflammation
meta_description: Researchers at UCL discovered how the body naturally stops inflammation, opening doors to safer treatments for chronic inflammatory diseases.
summary_short: UCL scientists uncovered epoxy-oxylipins, natural molecules that act as brakes on harmful immune cells, offering hope for chronic disease treatments.
body:
Researchers at University College London have identified a hidden biological mechanism that helps the body switch off inflammation—a discovery that could reshape treatment for millions suffering from chronic inflammatory diseases. The scientists found that small fat-derived molecules called epoxy-oxylipins naturally suppress intermediate monocytes, a type of white blood cell that can fuel persistent inflammation if left unchecked. In a landmark study published in Nature Communications, the team gave healthy volunteers injections of UV-killed bacteria in the forearm, then administered a drug called GSK2256294 to block an enzyme that normally breaks down these protective molecules. The results were striking: boosting epoxy-oxylipin levels eased pain faster and sharply reduced harmful immune cells in both blood and tissue, even when visible swelling and redness remained unchanged. This suggests the drug was healing inflammation at a deeper level than surface symptoms reveal.

What makes this finding significant is not just what it discovered, but what it reveals about how the body naturally heals. While scientists have long understood how inflammation starts, they've struggled to explain how the body knows when danger has passed and shifts from fighting to repairing. The new research maps that transition for the first time in humans. The study's design was careful: some volunteers received treatment before inflammation developed, while others received it four hours after symptoms appeared, mimicking real-world use. Both approaches worked equally well.

Many existing anti-inflammatory treatments suppress the immune system broadly, which can leave people vulnerable to infection. The epoxy-oxylipin pathway offers a different strategy—strengthening a process the body already uses. As Professor Derek Gilroy noted, GSK2256294 is already approved for human use, meaning it could potentially be repurposed quickly for chronic inflammatory flares. This research doesn't promise a cure, but it points toward safer medicines that work with the body's own defenses rather than against them.
quick_facts: University College London scientists identified epoxy-oxylipins as natural inflammation brakes
Drug GSK2256294 blocks enzyme that breaks down protective molecules
Study involved 48 healthy volunteers receiving UV-killed bacteria injections
Pain relief occurred faster with treatment in both early and late intervention
Findings published in Nature Communications, September 2026
